themeSwitch: Switch between light and dark mode
shLead: Let the others at the table scan the code. Everyone can then pick their own language.
title: Shithead in 3 minutes
sub: The card game from every hostel in the world. Read it once, play one round, done.
goal: The goal: Get rid of all your cards. The last person still holding cards is the Shithead – and shuffles for the next round.
setupLead: You need a standard 52-card deck without jokers and 2 to 5 players.
dealP: Everyone gets 9 cards in three layers.
setupAlt: In front of each player are three piles, each with one face-down and one face-up card, plus three cards in hand.
lgHand: 3 in your handonly you see them
setupP: Do not look at your face-down cards. The rest of the deck goes in the middle as the draw pile.
swLead: Before the first card is played, everyone may swap between their hand and their face-up cards. Once the game is running, you can’t anymore.
swAlt: The face-up 4 on the table is swapped with the ace from the hand.
w1p: Look at your 3 hand cards and your 3 face-up cards. The face-down ones stay face-down.
w2p: Swap as many cards between your hand and your face-up cards as you like.
w3p: In the end you have 3 face-up cards in front of you and 3 in your hand. Once everyone is done, the game starts.
swWhy: You only play your face-up cards at the very end, without a hand to fall back on. So put strong cards face-up: high cards like aces and kings, or special cards like the 2 and the 10. You’ll learn what the special cards do further down under special cards.
rankLead: The 2 is the lowest card, the ace the highest. Suits (♠♥♦♣) don’t matter.
rankAlt: Card order from low to high: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace.
rankP: J = Jack, Q = Queen, K = King, A = Ace.
turnLead: Look at the top card of the discard pile. Then there’s only one question:
dq: Do you have a card that’s equal or higher?
dqs: Special cards like the 2 or the 10 work almost always – more on that below.
by1: Play it face-up on the discard pile. You can play several of the same rank together, like three 6s.
by2: Draw until you have 3 cards in your hand again. If you still have 3 or more, you don’t draw.
bn1: Pick up the whole discard pile into your hand.
dnext: Either way, it’s then the next player’s turn, clockwise.
startP: Whoever has a 4 in their hand plays it and starts. If nobody has a 4, the next higher card starts, so a 5 and so on. After that, play goes clockwise.
spLead: These cards do something special. The 2, 3 and 10 can be played almost anytime, no matter what’s on top.
sp2p: Resets the pile. Any card can go on top of it.
sp3p: Doesn’t count. The next player has to beat the card under the 3.
sp7p: Only the next player must play a 7 or lower, or a 2, 3 or 10.
sp8p: You play it like a normal card. Then the next player misses a turn – with two 8s the next two players, and so on.
sp10p: The whole pile is out of the game. You go again right away.
sp4p: If four cards of the same rank are on top (even from different players), the pile burns too.
e1p: Then nobody draws anymore. You keep playing as usual, but your hand gets smaller with every turn. If you have to pick up the discard pile, you get more cards again, of course.
e2p: Only once the draw pile is gone and you have no cards left in your hand do you play from the table: first your face-up cards, then the face-down ones.
e3p: You play a face-up card just like one from your hand, and several of the same rank together. If you can’t play any, you pick up the discard pile and first play your hand empty again.
e4p: Tap one and flip it. If it fits, great. If not, you pick it up together with the discard pile and first play those empty again.
e5p: Once you’re out of cards, you’ve won. The last one at the table is the Shithead and deals the next round.
qLead: Quick test. One card is on top, you have one in your hand.
stLead: Once you know the rules, these help you win more often.
t1p: When swapping at the start, put aces, 10s and 2s face-up. You play those at the end without a hand – that’s when they need to hit.
t2p: Dump your 4s, 5s and 6s early while the pile is low. Later they won’t fit anywhere.
t3p: A 2 or a 10 is your emergency exit. Don’t waste it if you can play normally.
t4p: If your neighbor only has high cards face-up, a 7 forces them to pick up the pile.
t5p: A small pile early on barely hurts and often gives you good cards. A big one at the end is the problem.
t6p: Roughly track how many 10s and 2s are gone. Then you know when you can take a risk.
t7p: Playing matching cards together saves turns – and the fourth one burns the pile.
c1d: Get rid of all your cards.
c2d: Play equal or higher, draw back to 3.
c8bd: Next player misses a turn (one per 8).
c8d: Four of a kind burns too.
foot: Have fun at the table. And remember: you’re only the Shithead if you can’t laugh about it.

quiz.always2: A 2 can always be played – it resets the pile.
quiz.always3: A 3 can always be played – it’s invisible.
quiz.always10: A 10 can always be played – it burns the pile.
quiz.after7ok: After a 7 it has to be 7 or lower – fits.
quiz.after7no: After a 7 it has to be 7 or lower.
quiz.same: The same rank can always be played.
quiz.lower: {mine} is lower than {top} – you’d have to pick up the pile.

game.title: Play Shithead against bots
game.sub: Shithead against 1–4 computer players, right in your browser. Works offline too.
game.swapHint: Swap if you like: tap a hand card, then one of your face-up cards. Tap “Ready” when you’re done.
game.yourTurn: Your turn: play a card that’s equal or higher.
game.yourTurnSeven: Your turn: after the 7 it has to be 7 or lower.
game.yourTurnUp: Your hand is empty: play from your face-up cards.
game.yourTurnDown: Your turn: tap a face-down card to flip it.
game.noFit: Nothing fits – pick up the pile.
game.youBurn: The pile burns! You go again.
game.flipFail: {name} flips {cards} – no luck, picks up the pile.
game.youFlipFail: You flip {cards} – no luck, you pick up the pile.
game.ctaP: Play against 1–4 bots right here – they play by exactly these rules.
game.stalemate: Endless loop: the same cards keep going round and nobody can get out. It’s a draw!
